title: Léon: The Professional
tagline: Quiet man. Loud appetite. Lots of milk.
about: A solitary hitman takes in a 12-year-old girl after her family is killed.
cue: Pour a glass of milk every time Léon does.
faces: Ristorante. Lunch and dinner, every day.
Our block of Mulberry Street, 1900. Still feeding it.
San Marzano tomatoes crushed by hand, garlic cooked slow, basil and a knob of butter. Parmigiano on the side. Ask for Tony.
Ricotta, mozzarella and Sunday gravy, baked bubbling in its own dish.
Littleneck clams, garlic, white wine and parsley.
My regulars sit in the back, drink their milk and say nothing. Quiet people, I trust. Mangia.
The back table. Cold milk, checked cloth, no questions.
Crusty bread spread thick with sweet butter, thin boiled ham and little sour pickles, cut in twelve.
Warmed in oil with orange peel, thyme and garlic, with cornichons and pickled onions.
Chocolate mousse and cookie soil in a clay pot, a mint sprig growing out the top. Likes the sun.
Crisp shells filled to order with sweet ricotta and chocolate chips.
Milk, ice cream, malt and honey, frosted glass.
Whole, poured tall. A quart to go, 1.94.
By the glass, well chilled. Over eighteen only.
Prices subject to change. Thursday nights, a little Beethoven.
Mulberry St., New York, N.Y. 10013. Form 194. 1994.
